summary.business: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Limited acts as the investment manager to Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, one of India's largest mutual funds. The company provides long-term investment solutions across mutual funds, portfolio management services, alternative investment funds, real estate, and offshore offerings to retail and institutional investors. It leverages a multi-channel distribution network, digital platforms, and a pan-India presence to drive financial inclusion.

currentContext.strengths: Established multi-channel distribution network with over 310 locations covering 19,000+ pin codes, with >80% in B30 cities.|Strong retail franchise evidenced by 1.10 Crore folios and growing SIP book reaching ₹1,204 Crore in March 2026.|Diversified product suite spanning mutual funds and alternate assets, with a presence in the GIFT City IFSC for global strategies.|Robust risk management and governance framework with a three-lines-of-defence model.
currentContext.strategies: Focus on strengthening retail participation and deepening distribution reach across channels.|Leverage technology and digital platforms to enhance customer experience and operational efficiency.|Expand passive and alternative investment offerings to diversify product mix.|Maintain disciplined cost management while investing in brand and distribution.|Dividend policy: Board proposed a dividend of ₹25.50 per equity share for FY2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. No other capital allocation philosophy (buyback, debt reduction, credit rating, or reinvestment intent) was disclosed in the provided text.|Corporate governance framework with specialized Board Committees (Audit, Risk Management, Nomination Remuneration and Compensation, Stakeholders Relationship, CSR, Unit Holder Protection) and Enterprise Risk Management framework supported by regular internal audits.|Structured human capital development through leadership programs, continuous learning initiatives, performance management with differentiated rewards, and focus on workplace safety, mental health awareness, and POSH sensitization.|CSR implementation through participative approach with credible project implementing agencies, building project ownership within communities for project sustenance.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC International (IFSC) Limited (ABSLAMC IFSC), on 4th December 2025 in GIFT City, IFSC. ABSLAMC IFSC obtained Fund Management Entity – Retail registration from IFSCA and was set up to undertake fund management activities, including management of Alternative Investment Funds and global investment strategies. Pursuant to a Business Transfer Agreement dated 23rd March 2026, the Company transferred its GIFT City, IFSC Branch Fund Management business to ABSLAMC IFSC.
currentContext.mdna: Indian economy grew strongly in FY26 with real GDP estimated at 7.6%, making India the fastest growing major economy.|Consumption growth was healthy at 7.7%, supported by strong industrial and services sector performance.|Inflation was exceptionally benign in FY26, enabling RBI to cut repo rate by 75 bps and CRR by 100 bps.|Government remained committed to fiscal consolidation with fiscal deficit reduced to 4.4% of GDP.|India's economic outlook for FY27 remains broadly positive, though external risks from West Asia conflict and El Nino exist.|Domestic growth remains resilient with positive developments in trade talks with US and Europe.

risks.note: Sharp rise in US tariffs and trade policy uncertainty are clouding global capex decisions and supply-chain reorientation, which can affect capital flows into Indian markets and investor sentiment.

risks.risk: Energy supply shock and stagflationary pressures
risks.note: The 2026 Iran conflict has blocked 20% of world oil supply, creating a classic supply-side shock with stagflationary impulses that threaten to dent growth and heighten inflation, impacting market stability.

India's BoP deficit of US$30.8 bn in 9MFY26, driven by weak foreign capital inflows and sustained FDI repatriation, combined with US tariff concerns and the Iran conflict, is putting pressure on the INR and may affect foreign investment flows into mutual funds.

The likely development of El Nino weather conditions and IMD's forecast of a below-normal monsoon could negatively impact the economy, agricultural output, and food inflation, with knock-on effects on rural demand and market sentiment.

In the asset management industry, even perceived non-compliance, conflicts of interest, or governance lapses can erode investor trust, lead to regulatory penalties, client attrition, and weaker fund inflows, directly impacting AUM and revenue.

Attrition in critical roles or gaps in building future-ready capabilities can affect service quality and business continuity in a knowledge-driven business, with front-line attrition and skill gaps posing a direct risk to operational resilience.

one-line thesis: Solid-but-not-spectacular quarter: revenue +11% / PAT +12%, equity yield holding at 63–64 bps post the 1-Apr BER/TER reset (management calls it a "true picture" run-rate), and headline AUM optically supercharged by the low-fee EPFO mandate (~INR 6.08 lakh cr) pushing total AUM past INR 10 lakh cr. The real story is a **franchise-repair effort** — improved fund performance getting ABSL back onto bank recommendation lists (HDFC Bank, Kotak, StanChart, IndusInd) — set against a persistent drag: **SIP/market-share slippage** (ELSS outflows) and a still-sub-scale, if fast-growing, alternates/passive build-out.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue | INR 625 cr | +11% (from 565) | equity yield reset (BER) reflected |
| PBT | INR 406 cr | +9% (from 372) | — |
| PAT | INR 309 cr | +12% (from 277) | — |
| MF quarterly avg AUM | INR 4.28 lakh cr | +6% | equity MF ~INR 1.99 lakh cr (+10%); equity mix 46.5% |
| Overall avg AUM (incl alt) | INR 6.28 lakh cr | +42% | inflated by ESIC + EPFO (~1.5 months of EPFO in avg) |
| Closing total AUM | > INR 10 lakh cr | milestone | EPFO mandate ~INR 6.08 lakh cr added |
| SIP monthly contribution (Jun) | INR 1,085 cr | — | 40 lakh SIP folios; 5.5 lakh new SIP regs in Q1; SIP AUM ~INR 87,000 cr |
| Passive avg AUM | ~INR 40,000 cr | +14% | ETF AUM +47% YoY (vs industry +29%); 52 passive products; 17.4 lakh folios |
| PMS + AIF assets | ~INR 2 lakh cr | from INR 28,650 cr | **includes EPFO flows** — ex-mandate alternates still sub-scale |
> Employee cost stepped up on ESOP (rolled out eff. Jan-2026): ~INR 10 cr/quarter incremental, to persist. Total employees 1,638. Yields: equity 63–64 bps, debt 24–25 bps, liquid 12–13 bps, ETF ~8 bps. PMS+AIF = ~7% of gross revenue / ~4% of net revenue. Fixed-income AUM took a temporary May hit (rate volatility) that reversed by June-end/July.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Yields:** hold at current levels going forward (equity ~63–64 bps) barring 1–2 bps and **telescoping pricing** as AUM scales; BER reset is fully rolled out.
- **PMS long-only equity:** grow from ~INR 5,000 cr to **INR 20,000–21,000 cr over ~3 years**.
- **AIF Performing Credit + AIF Money Market:** each to target **INR 5,000–7,000 cr** initially; AMC to seed **up to 10% of fund size** + provide bridge capital.
- **Alternates revenue contribution:** stay in similar range (±1–2%); "all LOBs firing."
- **OPEX:** within inflationary guidelines; employee cost flat-ish at Q1 run-rate (ESOP absorbed); "no cost shocks."
- **GIFT City:** launch retail products **next quarter** (emerging-market equity fund, India growth fund, global index funds) — inbound + outbound.
- **SIF:** two more launches — Equity Long-Short and Equity Ex-Top-100 Long-Short (adding to the live Apex SIF Hybrid Long-Short).
order book & pipeline:
- Product pipeline: GIFT City retail suite (next quarter), 2 new SIFs, ABSL Select Sector Fund / Structured Opportunity Fund II / Money Manager Fund / India Select Sector Fund / Special Opportunity Fund Series II (PMS/AIF), Real-Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II (senior-secured, brownfield Tier-1).
- Distribution "pipeline": flagship funds newly added to bank recommendation lists — HDFC Bank (FlexiCap, last 2 weeks), Kotak, StanChart, IndusInd, YES Securities/YES Bank, LGT Wealth, Ask Wealth — flow uplift expected to follow.
- EPFO gateway: mandate opens door to ~1,350 EPFO trusts for equity-contribution flows into ABSL active + passive funds (early-stage).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Active equity (core):** 7–8 flagship "focus" funds (FlexiCap, Balanced Advantage, Multi-Asset Allocation, Small Cap, Multicap, MidCap, PSU Equity) seeing improved flows; performance improvement across short and medium-to-long term is the pitch.
- **Fixed income:** large duration/non-liquid book; May rate panic caused temporary AUM dip, fully reversed by June-end/July.
- **Passive/ETF:** strategic focus; new Head of Passives (Hemen Bhatia, 2 decades) + team; ETF growing well ahead of industry; low-margin but absolute-profit-additive.
- **Alternates:** three buckets — PMS long-only equity (~INR 5,000 cr), AIF (Performing Credit ~14% delivered, Money Market, Real-Estate Credit), and GIFT City offshore; ~INR 700 cr real-estate AUM (+25%).
growth verticals / optionality:
- **GIFT City retail license:** platform for domestic-savings diversification into global equities (outbound) + NRI feeder inflows (inbound); management "bullish," scalable offshore franchise over coming years.
- **EPFO/ESIC mandates:** near-zero direct revenue but a strategic wedge — credibility + a channel to EPFO trusts' equity money.
- **SIF (specialised investment funds):** new regulatory category; long-short platform being scaled after 6-month track-record build.
- **Passive leadership build:** new team + 52-product suite as the structural-shift hedge.
margins & cost dynamics:
- Equity yield 63–64 bps is the post-BER steady state; telescoping pricing will slowly compress blended yield as AUM grows, partly offset by alternates mix. Passive/GIFT City are deliberately low-margin, absolute-profit plays.
- Cost side: ESOP adds ~INR 10 cr/quarter; otherwise inflationary. Fee-and-commission expense scales with alternates/PMS distribution payouts.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - Asset-light. "Expansion" = product launches + team hires (Passives head, SIF specialists) + AMC seed/bridge capital into own AIFs (up to 10% of fund size) + tech (Gen-AI chatbot, new distributor/investor app, WhatsApp servicing).
capital allocation: - AMC P&L commits seed capital (≤10% of fund size) + temporary bridge capital to launch/scale alternates — a modest own-balance-sheet deployment to seed the higher-fee alternates franchise. No buyback/dividend commentary this call.
risks & watch-items:
- **SIP / market-share slippage** — sequential SIP-share decline; ELSS outflows + elevated industry cancellation rates; SIP book saw a "marginal reduction." The core structural worry.
- **Ex-mandate non-MF book stagnant** — an analyst flagged the alternates book (ex EPFO/ESIC) has been roughly flat for ~3 years despite new teams; execution-to-scale is unproven.
- **Passive/ETF structural fee compression** — industry mix shift + telescoping pricing pressure blended yields over time.
- **AUM optics** — the +42% AUM / >INR 10 lakh cr headline is heavily EPFO-mandate driven at near-zero yield; revenue growth (+11%) is the honest read.
- **Flow concentration** in a handful of flagship funds; recommendation-list additions are recent and unproven at scale.
management quality / tone: CEO Balasubramanian candid and hands-on — described personally doing a distributor "Yatra" across cities, admitted SIP/ELSS softness and the ex-mandate alternates flatness rather than deflecting, and repeatedly framed the turnaround as "give it time / it comes on auto mode once established." Realistic on EPFO revenue ("very marginal… doesn't add much"). CFO Sharma precise on yields, ESOP quantum, employee count. Tone is credible-rebuild, not hype; but several answers were qualitative where analysts pressed for quantified market-share/flow data.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The AUM headline is misleading:** +42% AUM and >INR 10 lakh cr are EPFO/ESIC-mandate optics at negligible yield — real economics are the +11% revenue / +12% PAT and the 63–64 bps equity yield.
- **BER/TER reset was a non-event to yields** — the 1-Apr commission restructuring was engineered "neutral/win-win," so yields held rather than compressed (a relief vs feared TER drag).
- **Bank recommendation-list re-entry** (HDFC Bank FlexiCap added in the last 2 weeks; Kotak, StanChart, IndusInd) is the single most watchable flow catalyst — performance has re-qualified ABSL products that had dropped off comparison lists.
- **EPFO is a strategic option, not a P&L event** — its value is the gateway to ~1,350 trusts, not the mandate fee.
- Alternates (PMS→INR 20–21k cr target, AIFs→INR 5–7k cr each) are the stated margin-mix upgrade, but ex-mandate the book has been flat for 3 years — the credibility gap to close.

> AMC call — mostly firm-specific flow/turnaround dynamics. One genuine sector-structural theme (active→passive shift + fee compression). Kept minimal to avoid padding.

| "a lot of manufacturers are focusing on the passive side and the ETF side" + telescoping pricing → structural fee compression for active AMCs | Passive-scaled AMCs incl. **HDFCAMC · 541729** / **NAM-INDIA (Nippon) · 540767** ⭐ (and ABSLAMC's own ETF push, +47%) | Sub-scale active-only AMCs (incl. peer **CRAMC · 544580**, small active-led) | Scale + low-cost wins passive; ABSL is building it but late; **Low–Med** ⭐ sector-knowledge, not named by mgmt |
| SIP/ELSS market-share slippage; flows migrating to funds on bank recommendation lists | Distribution-strong AMCs / bank-channel AMCs ⭐ | ABSLAMC (self, on SIP share) | Recommendation-list presence drives flows; ABSL only now re-qualifying; **Med** (self, ✅ discussed) |

Total AUM > INR 10 L cr incl EPFO (~INR 6.08 L cr) + ESIC. SIP contribution INR 1,085 cr/mo, SIP AUM ~INR 87,000 cr; SIP/ELSS share slipped. Equity yield 63–64 bps post-BER (stable). ESOP +~INR 10 cr/qtr. Passive avg AUM ~INR 40,000 cr (+14%), ETF +47%. PMS+AIF ~INR 2 L cr (incl EPFO). Employees 1,638. Guidance: PMS long-only INR 20–21k cr in 3 yrs; AIF Performing Credit & Money Market INR 5–7k cr each; GIFT City retail launch next qtr; 2 new SIFs; yields held; opex inflationary.

business_model.body: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Limited acts as the investment manager to Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, one of India's largest mutual funds. The company provides long-term investment solutions across mutual funds, portfolio management services, alternative investment funds, real estate, and offshore offerings to retail and institutional investors. It leverages a multi-channel distribution network, digital platforms, and a pan-India presence to drive financial inclusion.

- Subsidiary Companies (unnamed in provided text) — subsidiary: ESOP Scheme 2021, ESOP Scheme 2025, and SAR 2022 benefits extended to employees of subsidiaries

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Active equity (core):** 7–8 flagship "focus" funds (FlexiCap, Balanced Advantage, Multi-Asset Allocation, Small Cap, Multicap, MidCap, PSU Equity) seeing improved flows; performance improvement across short and medium-to-long term is the pitch.
- **Fixed income:** large duration/non-liquid book; May rate panic caused temporary AUM dip, fully reversed by June-end/July.
- **Passive/ETF:** strategic focus; new Head of Passives (Hemen Bhatia, 2 decades) + team; ETF growing well ahead of industry; low-margin but absolute-profit-additive.
- **Alternates:** three buckets — PMS long-only equity (~INR 5,000 cr), AIF (Performing Credit ~14% delivered, Money Market, Real-Estate Credit), and GIFT City offshore; ~INR 700 cr real-estate AUM (+25%).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Mutual Funds:** Equity Funds, Debt Funds, Liquid Funds, ETF
- **Alternate Assets:** Portfolio Management Services (PMS), Alternative Investment Funds (AIF), Real Estate Investments, Offshore Offerings

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Product pipeline: GIFT City retail suite (next quarter), 2 new SIFs, ABSL Select Sector Fund / Structured Opportunity Fund II / Money Manager Fund / India Select Sector Fund / Special Opportunity Fund Series II (PMS/AIF), Real-Estate Credit Opportunities Fund Series II (senior-secured, brownfield Tier-1).
- Distribution "pipeline": flagship funds newly added to bank recommendation lists — HDFC Bank (FlexiCap, last 2 weeks), Kotak, StanChart, IndusInd, YES Securities/YES Bank, LGT Wealth, Ask Wealth — flow uplift expected to follow.
- EPFO gateway: mandate opens door to ~1,350 EPFO trusts for equity-contribution flows into ABSL active + passive funds (early-stage).

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Yields:** hold at current levels going forward (equity ~63–64 bps) barring 1–2 bps and **telescoping pricing** as AUM scales; BER reset is fully rolled out.
- **PMS long-only equity:** grow from ~INR 5,000 cr to **INR 20,000–21,000 cr over ~3 years**.
- **AIF Performing Credit + AIF Money Market:** each to target **INR 5,000–7,000 cr** initially; AMC to seed **up to 10% of fund size** + provide bridge capital.
- **Alternates revenue contribution:** stay in similar range (±1–2%); "all LOBs firing."
- **OPEX:** within inflationary guidelines; employee cost flat-ish at Q1 run-rate (ESOP absorbed); "no cost shocks."
- **GIFT City:** launch retail products **next quarter** (emerging-market equity fund, India growth fund, global index funds) — inbound + outbound.
- **SIF:** two more launches — Equity Long-Short and Equity Ex-Top-100 Long-Short (adding to the live Apex SIF Hybrid Long-Short).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **GIFT City retail license:** platform for domestic-savings diversification into global equities (outbound) + NRI feeder inflows (inbound); management "bullish," scalable offshore franchise over coming years.
- **EPFO/ESIC mandates:** near-zero direct revenue but a strategic wedge — credibility + a channel to EPFO trusts' equity money.
- **SIF (specialised investment funds):** new regulatory category; long-short platform being scaled after 6-month track-record build.
- **Passive leadership build:** new team + 52-product suite as the structural-shift hedge.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian economy grew strongly in FY26 with real GDP estimated at 7.6%, making India the fastest growing major economy.
- Consumption growth was healthy at 7.7%, supported by strong industrial and services sector performance.
- Inflation was exceptionally benign in FY26, enabling RBI to cut repo rate by 75 bps and CRR by 100 bps.
- Government remained committed to fiscal consolidation with fiscal deficit reduced to 4.4% of GDP.
- India's economic outlook for FY27 remains broadly positive, though external risks from West Asia conflict and El Nino exist.
- Domestic growth remains resilient with positive developments in trade talks with US and Europe.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Equity yield 63–64 bps is the post-BER steady state; telescoping pricing will slowly compress blended yield as AUM grows, partly offset by alternates mix. Passive/GIFT City are deliberately low-margin, absolute-profit plays.
- Cost side: ESOP adds ~INR 10 cr/quarter; otherwise inflationary. Fee-and-commission expense scales with alternates/PMS distribution payouts.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: - AMC P&L commits seed capital (≤10% of fund size) + temporary bridge capital to launch/scale alternates — a modest own-balance-sheet deployment to seed the higher-fee alternates franchise. No buyback/dividend commentary this call.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC International (IFSC) Limited (ABSLAMC IFSC), on 4th December 2025 in GIFT City, IFSC. ABSLAMC IFSC obtained Fund Management Entity – Retail registration from IFSCA and was set up to undertake fund management activities, including management of Alternative Investment Funds and global investment strategies. Pursuant to a Business Transfer Agreement dated 23rd March 2026, the Company transferred its GIFT City, IFSC Branch Fund Management business to ABSLAMC IFSC.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: CEO Balasubramanian candid and hands-on — described personally doing a distributor "Yatra" across cities, admitted SIP/ELSS softness and the ex-mandate alternates flatness rather than deflecting, and repeatedly framed the turnaround as "give it time / it comes on auto mode once established." Realistic on EPFO revenue ("very marginal… doesn't add much"). CFO Sharma precise on yields, ESOP quantum, employee count. Tone is credible-rebuild, not hype; but several answers were qualitative where analysts pressed for quantified market-share/flow data.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "No material litigation disclosed in the provided annual report text.", "as_of": "2026-07-03"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established multi-channel distribution network with over 310 locations covering 19,000+ pin codes, with >80% in B30 cities.
- Strong retail franchise evidenced by 1.10 Crore folios and growing SIP book reaching ₹1,204 Crore in March 2026.
- Diversified product suite spanning mutual funds and alternate assets, with a presence in the GIFT City IFSC for global strategies.
- Robust risk management and governance framework with a three-lines-of-defence model.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **SIP / market-share slippage** — sequential SIP-share decline; ELSS outflows + elevated industry cancellation rates; SIP book saw a "marginal reduction." The core structural worry.
- **Ex-mandate non-MF book stagnant** — an analyst flagged the alternates book (ex EPFO/ESIC) has been roughly flat for ~3 years despite new teams; execution-to-scale is unproven.
- **Passive/ETF structural fee compression** — industry mix shift + telescoping pricing pressure blended yields over time.
- **AUM optics** — the +42% AUM / >INR 10 lakh cr headline is heavily EPFO-mandate driven at near-zero yield; revenue growth (+11%) is the honest read.
- **Flow concentration** in a handful of flagship funds; recommendation-list additions are recent and unproven at scale.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The AUM headline is misleading:** +42% AUM and >INR 10 lakh cr are EPFO/ESIC-mandate optics at negligible yield — real economics are the +11% revenue / +12% PAT and the 63–64 bps equity yield.
- **BER/TER reset was a non-event to yields** — the 1-Apr commission restructuring was engineered "neutral/win-win," so yields held rather than compressed (a relief vs feared TER drag).
- **Bank recommendation-list re-entry** (HDFC Bank FlexiCap added in the last 2 weeks; Kotak, StanChart, IndusInd) is the single most watchable flow catalyst — performance has re-qualified ABSL products that had dropped off comparison lists.
- **EPFO is a strategic option, not a P&L event** — its value is the gateway to ~1,350 trusts, not the mandate fee.
- Alternates (PMS→INR 20–21k cr target, AIFs→INR 5–7k cr each) are the stated margin-mix upgrade, but ex-mandate the book has been flat for 3 years — the credibility gap to close.

challenges.body:

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** Revenue INR 625 cr (+11%), PBT INR 406 cr (+9%), PAT INR 309 cr (+12%). MF avg AUM INR 4.28 L cr (+6%); equity MF ~INR 1.99 L cr (+10%, mix 46.5%). Total AUM > INR 10 L cr incl EPFO (~INR 6.08 L cr) + ESIC. SIP contribution INR 1,085 cr/mo, SIP AUM ~INR 87,000 cr; SIP/ELSS share slipped. Equity yield 63–64 bps post-BER (stable). ESOP +~INR 10 cr/qtr. Passive avg AUM ~INR 40,000 cr (+14%), ETF +47%. PMS+AIF ~INR 2 L cr (incl EPFO). Employees 1,638. Guidance: PMS long-only INR 20–21k cr in 3 yrs; AIF Performing Credit & Money Market INR 5–7k cr each; GIFT City retail launch next qtr; 2 new SIFs; yields held; opex inflationary.
- _next → check: SIP/ELSS flow-share stabilising or still slipping; whether bank recommendation-list additions (HDFC Bank FlexiCap etc.) convert to visible equity inflows; equity yield holding 63–64 bps vs telescoping drag; alternates ex-mandate actually scaling (PMS toward INR 20k cr); GIFT City product launches shipped; PMS+AIF ex-EPFO growth._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Labour Codes] India's four new Labour Codes took effect 21 November 2025; the company recognised a Rs 2.82 crore incremental charge under exceptional items for FY26 and will account for further impact once the related rules are notified.
- [Mandate concentration] The 5x jump in PMS/AIF AUM is driven almost entirely by ESIC and EPFO mandates (INR 1,898 bn of the INR 1,945 bn), which are institutional and likely lower-yield than retail assets.
- [SIF] The deck introduces Mutual Fund - SIF as a separate AUM line within equity reporting, indicating entry into the Specialised Investment Fund category.
